I have farmed a long time, so I do not like to spread myself too thin on only 5 mu. Since some people in my family work off-farm, I need a plan that is steady, familiar, and not too labor-heavy at peak times. I also have well irrigation, so I will use that to protect yield, but I still want to control costs. Because my cropping pattern is centered on cotton, I will keep most of the land in cotton and leave smaller areas for wheat and maize. For cotton, I will use improved seed, not the cheapest traditional seed, because cotton has higher value on my farm and I want more stable emergence and boll setting. I will fertilize cotton a bit more heavily than the grain crops, irrigate several times through key stages, and use rotary tillage because it is practical and saves labor. For wheat, I will keep a smaller area for grain and household security, use improved seed, apply moderate fertilizer, and irrigate at the main water-demand stages. For maize, I will also keep a small area, use hybrid seed because maize responds well and is dependable, and manage it with moderate fertilizer and fewer irrigations than cotton. I will not chase the highest possible input level. At my age, with 40 years of experience, I care more about a manageable workload, stable output, and avoiding unnecessary spending.
